solved_when: A protein-functionalized separator is demonstrated through 1,000 capture–release cycles while retaining at least 90% of its useful separation performance, with realistic contaminants and regeneration conditions included in the protocol.
why: Protein replacement and regeneration can govern the economics of biologically inspired separation; without long lifetimes, reusable protein separators cannot compete as practical separation platforms.
key_works: Q. Ye et al. (2025), *Group Separation of Rare Earth Elements by Protein-Functionalized Magnetic Nanoparticles*, DOI:10.1021/acsestengg.5c00508.

title: Ten-thousand-cycle qualification of COF air-capture sorbents
open: Can a covalent organic framework sorbent for direct air capture survive long-term field use, retaining nearly all of its working capacity over its lifetime? The proposed qualification target is 10,000 representative capture–regeneration cycles with less than 10% loss of usable capacity, tested under real-air contaminants and in mechanically shaped (not powdered) material.
status: Research on COF-999 (Zhou et al., 2024, DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08080-x) includes approximately one hundred-cycle laboratory durability evidence, which is encouraging but does not establish the proposed 10,000-cycle target. A related open issue is accelerated-life extrapolation when failure modes evolve chemically over time.
solved_when: A mechanically shaped COF sorbent completes 10,000 representative capture–regeneration cycles — including exposure to real-air contaminants — while losing less than 10% of its usable capacity.
why: Sorbent replacement frequency can determine both the capture cost and the lifecycle environmental burden of direct air capture, so a long-lived sorbent is what makes the economics and sustainability case credible.
key_works: Zhou et al. (2024), COF-999 capture study, DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08080-x.

title: Exact nested-surface, non-axisymmetric vacuum fields
open: Can an exact vacuum magnetic field with nontrivial rotational transform and globally nested invariant surfaces exist in a toroidal region of ordinary three-dimensional space without axisymmetry? Either construct such a field analytically, or establish the obstruction that rules it out.
status: Special constructions on a topological torus and approximate numerical configurations exist; Weitzner and Sengupta (2020) gave exact non-symmetric closed-line vacuum fields in a topological torus (*Physics of Plasmas* 27, 022509). The 2026 analytic pressure-supported equilibria of Landreman (arXiv:2609.26742) do not automatically supply the corresponding vacuum-field construction.
solved_when: An explicit analytic non-axisymmetric vacuum field in a torus embedded in ordinary three-dimensional space is constructed, possessing globally nested invariant surfaces and nontrivial rotational transform; alternatively, a rigorous proof of the relevant obstruction is given.
why: It would clarify which magnetic-confinement geometries can exist without plasma-current assistance.
key_works: W. Weitzner and W. Sengupta (2020), *Exact non-symmetric closed line vacuum magnetic fields in a topological torus*, Physics of Plasmas 27, 022509; Landreman (2026), arXiv:2609.26742.

title: Thermally isolated micrometre gaps that remain dimensionally stable
open: Can a micrometre-scale vacuum gap be held dimensionally stable at extreme temperatures? The goal is to realize a 1–4 μm gap over a square-centimetre active area at temperatures above 1,500 K, with spacer conductance below approximately 10 mW cm⁻² K⁻¹ and no progressive gap collapse.
status: Micrometre-gap converters exist; the roadmap (Bellucci et al. (2026), thermionic roadmap, DOI:10.1088/1361-6463/ae611e) identifies support conduction and dimensional stability as coupled constraints.
solved_when: A device demonstrates a 1–4 μm gap sustained over a square-centimetre active area above 1,500 K, with spacer thermal conductance below ~10 mW cm⁻² K⁻¹ and no progressive gap collapse.
why: Reducing space charge in thermionic converters by narrowing the gap must not come at the cost of overwhelming conductive heat leakage through the spacers.
key_works: Bellucci et al. (2026), thermionic roadmap, DOI:10.1088/1361-6463/ae611e.

title: Experimental multijunction thermoradiative advantage
open: Does stacking junctions actually pay off in a thermoradiative device? Demonstrate experimentally that a multijunction thermoradiative device outperforms a comparable single-junction device once interconnection, optical coupling, and thermal losses are all accounted for.
status: A 2025 idealized analysis (P. Bohm, A. K. Menon, and Z. M. Zhang, *Fundamental advantages of multijunction thermoradiative cells*, DOI:10.1063/5.0273591) predicts relative efficiency and power improvements at a 500 K emitter and 300 K sink, but these remain calculated gains; no multijunction experiment has been completed.
solved_when: A working multijunction thermoradiative device is built and measured to deliver higher net efficiency and/or power output than a comparable single-junction device under realistic operating conditions, with all interconnection, optical coupling, and thermal losses included in the accounting.
why: It establishes whether junction complexity produces a net benefit, converting an idealized theoretical prediction into a demonstrated capability (or a documented failure) for thermoradiative power conversion.
key_works: P. Bohm, A. K. Menon, and Z. M. Zhang (2025), *Fundamental advantages of multijunction thermoradiative cells*, DOI:10.1063/5.0273591.

title: Experimental separation of spin Thomson heating
open: Can an experiment detect the reversible heating or cooling that is proportional to both a spin current and a temperature gradient — the spin-dependent analogue of Thomson heating — and separate the electron-mediated from the magnon-mediated contributions when both channels are present?
status: The spin-dependent Thomson responses currently have theoretical descriptions, but the May 2026 experimental perspective of Uchida and Hirai (2026), *Spin caloritronics: History and future prospects of experiments*, arXiv:2605.01692, identifies their observation as unresolved; earlier modeling of thermal spin transport and spin-orbit effects in ferromagnetic/nonmagnetic mesoscopic devices appears in A. Slachter et al. (2011), DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.84.174408.
solved_when: A measurement demonstrates reversible heating or cooling scaling jointly with spin current and temperature gradient, and cleanly distinguishes electron-mediated from magnon-mediated contributions in a regime where both mechanisms can operate.
why: It would determine whether distributed spin-dependent heating can supplement interface-localized thermal control in spin caloritronic devices.
key_works: Uchida and Hirai (2026), *Spin caloritronics: History and future prospects of experiments*, arXiv:2605.01692; A. Slachter et al. (2011), *Modeling of thermal spin transport and spin-orbit effects in ferromagnetic/nonmagnetic mesoscopic devices*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.84.174408.

title: Thousand-cycle retention for electrocatalytically discharged photoswitches
open: Can an electrocatalytically discharged photoswitch molecular-storage system retain at least 90% of its usable storage capacity after 1,000 complete charging–discharging cycles, with catalyst and electrolyte aging included?
status: High single-discharge selectivity has been reported for selected substituents (Franz et al. 2025, DOI:10.1002/chem.202502294), but no result yet determines cumulative full-cycle retention; trace-product accumulation and reliability of cyclic reaction networks remain related open concerns.
solved_when: A demonstrated system completes 1,000 full charge–discharge cycles while retaining at least 90% of its initial usable storage capacity, accounting for cumulative catalyst and electrolyte degradation.
why: Even small irreversible losses per cycle compound over repeated reuse, so high single-discharge performance does not translate into a practical, long-lived storage material.
key_works: Franz et al. (2025), electrocatalytic molecular-storage study, DOI:10.1002/chem.202502294.
